page: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g-240s is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided by a bundled 240 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top tier. However, multi-threaded performance scales moderately, with multi-core stress-ng and PassMark CPU scores falling into the average tier, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth remains stable in the average tier, reaching 440.06 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 70.96 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

This hardware configuration is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and database operations, as demonstrated by its average-tier Redis SET performance of 8.1 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 14.81 GB/sec. It is also capable of handling lightweight machine learning tasks, such as text generation on small 135M parameter models, though prompt processing on larger 7B models is poor. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores and NVMe storage provide a cost-effective, predictable resource profile for production applications requiring consistent CPU performance without the overhead of GPU acceleration.
description: The Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g-240s is a general-purpose virtual server from the VX1 Cloud Compute family, powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores, 2 threads per core) operating at 2.0 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 240 GB NVMe SSD. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression speeds, while multi-core operations, memory bandwidth, and database performance align with average-tier expectations. With a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance is optimized for workloads such as static web serving, database operations, and general-purpose application hosting.
